papers.title: Sleep fragmentation drives local, network-specific epileptic activity in human epilepsy
papers.summary: Using combined stereo-EEG and polysomnography in patients with epilepsy, this study found that experimentally induced sleep arousals cause rapid, local increases in interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) confined to neocortical regions, with a larger effect in N2 than N3 sleep. Arousals did not alter IED spatial propagation, suggesting state-dependent enhancement of local cortical excitability without broader network recruitment.

papers.title: Human P301L tau expression in mice alters neuronal excitability independent of neurodegeneration.
papers.summary: Expressing human P301L tau in mice produced increased EEG power in higher frequency bands from 3 months of age, with abnormal 40 Hz auditory steady-state responses and increased inter-trial coherence at 10 months, independent of age-dependent AT8 tau aggregates and neuroinflammation. The findings suggest that P301L tau alters neuronal excitability via disrupted physiological tau function rather than aggregate accumulation.

papers.title: Emergent multiscale organisation of neural dynamics fragments in anaesthesia.
papers.summary: Using dynamical independence on source-reconstructed EEG from humans under propofol, xenon, and ketamine anaesthesia, the study found that propofol and xenon increased emergence but fragmented macroscopic dynamical organisation, while ketamine reduced overall emergence yet partially preserved macroscopic structure. The results dissociate emergence from the organisation of emergent dynamics and indicate that wakeful consciousness depends on integration across scales.

papers.title: Exploiting frontotemporal asymmetry in low-channel EEG emotion recognition via spectral fusion network.
papers.summary: The paper proposes the Spatiotemporal Spectral Asymmetric Fusion Network (STSANet), a dual-branch model that explicitly quantifies frontotemporal hemispheric asymmetry and fuses spectral oscillations for low-channel EEG emotion recognition. It achieved accuracies of 86.80% on SEED and 87.43% on a self-collected dataset, with robustness in trial-level cross-validation and confirmed dependence on spatial asymmetry modeling.

papers.title: Imbalance-aware spectral classification via logit-label adjustment and multi-expert mutual learning.
papers.summary: Spec-ImC is an imbalance-aware spectral classification framework combining Logit-Label Adjustment, Cosine-Annealed Data Augmentation with Consistency Regularization, and Multi-Expert Mutual Learning to handle long-tailed molecular vibrational spectroscopy data. Extensive experiments on bacterial and cancer spectral datasets showed consistent state-of-the-art performance across simulated imbalance scenarios, especially improving few-shot class recognition.

papers.title: A significant enrichment that is not: spatial nulls, co-expression, and the imaging transcriptomics of EEG alpha-power genetics
papers.summary: This imaging transcriptomics study tested whether alpha-power-associated genes are enriched in cortical alpha generators and found that a field-standard spin test suggested enrichment (continuous p_spin = 0.022), but the signal was not band-specific, did not replicate across alpha phenotypes, and was unremarkable against matched random gene sets (p_geneset = 0.33). No result survived FDR correction across 24 tests (minimum q = 0.127), demonstrating that a spin-significant, surrogate-corroborated enrichment can be fully explained by gene-set co-expression.

papers.title: Individual SMR neurofeedback responsiveness during a single session and its associations with autonomic regulation and shooting performance in elite rifle athletes.
papers.summary: In a single-session exploratory study with 13 elite air rifle athletes, SMR neurofeedback responsiveness was indexed by amplitude slope, classifying 9 as Responders and 4 as Non-Responders. Responders showed larger post-training increases in DFA α2 and decreases in logLF, but associations with shooting performance and autonomic regulation did not survive FDR correction, so findings are hypothesis-generating.

papers.title: 20 Hz tACS engages striatal THINs to enhance β-band synchrony and motor drive.
papers.summary: In 18-month-old male mice, 20 Hz tACS over M1 for 7 days under sevoflurane anesthesia was associated with higher post-anesthesia reaching success, increased β-band power, elevated striatal dopamine release, and enhanced striatal THIN activation compared with sham. Optogenetic THIN activation recapitulated motor improvement and β-band enhancement, while THIN inhibition reduced successful attempts and β-band power, implicating striatal dopamine, THINs, and β-band synchrony in post-anesthesia motor recovery.

papers.title: Frequency-specific dynamic characteristics of brain networks during salt taste perception: an EEG-based functional and effective connectivity analysis.
papers.summary: This EEG study examined functional and effective connectivity during salt taste perception in 20 healthy participants across water and five NaCl concentrations. Salt stimulation enhanced whole-brain and inter-subnetwork phase synchronization, with the strongest PLV response at low concentration, and low-intensity salty stimulation increased beta-band effective connectivity from the gustatory perception subnetwork to the multisensory integration subnetwork.

papers.title: Central Mechanisms of Electroacupuncture in Chronic Heart Failure: Insights from Quantitative Proteomics of the Nucleus Tractus Solitarius.
papers.summary: Using a rat model of chronic heart failure, this study investigated central mechanisms of electroacupuncture at HT7 acupoints via quantitative proteomics of the nucleus tractus solitarius. Electroacupuncture improved cardiac function, restored NTS neuronal activity, and modulated 85 differentially expressed proteins, identifying YY1 as a candidate target associated with central neuromodulation.

papers.title: Retrospective attention reveals a decaying theta rhythm in conscious access to a preceding stimulus.
papers.summary: This study tested competing models of retroperception temporal dynamics using a retro-cue paradigm with dense behavioral sampling, spectral analysis, and computational modeling. Behavioral accuracy and subjective visibility showed theta-band fluctuations, with model comparison modestly favoring a damped oscillatory profile, suggesting conscious access to recent sensory information is rhythmically structured and temporally limited.

papers.title: Voice and linguistic features support early attentional filtering of irrelevant stimuli
papers.summary: In this EEG study, listeners attended to a lateralized stream of target syllables while ignoring distractors, which varied in voice and linguistic content. Both voice and linguistic dissimilarity independently and additively enhanced early target-evoked EEG responses and supported target recall, demonstrating that high-level linguistic features support early attentional filtering of irrelevant stimuli.

papers.title: Beyond single-person paradigms: N400 alterations in a social context in schizophrenia.
papers.summary: This EEG hyperscanning study examined the N400 ERP component in a social context using an actor-observer Go/NoGo task in patients with schizophrenia and healthy controls. Patients showed reduced N400 amplitudes overall and specifically to negative and positive stimuli, with N400 declining upon second stimulus exposure and higher PANSS scores associated with attenuated N400 amplitudes.

papers.title: Tracing the epistemic arc: Distinct physiological signatures for curiosity, insight, understanding and liking when viewing visual art
papers.summary: Two preregistered experiments used the 'title effect' with visual art to trace an epistemic arc from curiosity to insight (aha), understanding, and liking. Behavioral (N=55) and multimodal (EEG, ECG, eye tracking; N=49) data showed that understanding and curiosity were decodable from physiological signals, aha was decodable from pupil size but not EEG, and a fast initial EEG response linked to aesthetic liking.

papers.title: Electrophysiological dissociation of human posterior cingulate cortex contributions to value- and memory-based decision-making.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study recorded local field potentials and single units from human posterior cingulate cortex during matched value- and memory-based decision tasks. Dorsal but not ventral PCC showed sustained engagement across both tasks, with single-unit activity more temporally circumscribed, and dorsal PCC engagement extended to memory encoding, recognition, and confidence judgments, revealing a functional dissociation.

papers.title: [Tailoring care to the mind: The emerging role of artificial intelligence in precision psychiatry. Part I: Understanding, measuring and modelling clinical singularity].
papers.summary: This narrative review examines how artificial intelligence can support precision psychiatry by integrating multimodal data (clinical, biological, neuroimaging, digital) and modeling individual trajectories. It concludes that AI may enable dynamic, transdiagnostic patient profiling and adaptive treatment strategies, but clinical value depends on robust conceptual frameworks and data quality, and that most models identify associations rather than causal relationships.

papers.title: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy pre-ictal oscillations recorded simultaneously with stereo-EEG.
papers.summary: Using simultaneous fNIRS and stereo-EEG in five patients with 16 analyzable seizures, the study found that ultra-slow hemodynamic oscillations (0.002-0.004 Hz) preceded SEEG-defined seizure onset in three patients and 10 seizures, more often than expected by chance. The findings suggest a pre-ictal hemodynamic component, though the physiological origin and clinical significance remain uncertain.

papers.title: Narcolepsy-like presentations in intellectual disability with comorbid epilepsy and obstructive sleep apnea: a case-based diagnostic analysis and literature-informed discussion.
papers.summary: A case-based diagnostic analysis of a 34-year-old woman with intellectual disability, epilepsy, and obstructive sleep apnea presenting with excessive daytime sleepiness and nocturnal events, illustrating diagnostic overshadowing. After diagnosis via polysomnography, MSLT, and EEG, concurrent levetiracetam and CPAP therapy eliminated nocturnal episodes and improved Epworth Sleepiness Scale from 18 to 6 at 6 months.

papers.title: Analysis of pediatric absence epilepsy electroencephalograms using a mining-based association rule approach: A cross-sectional study based on realistic data.
papers.summary: Applied association rule mining to clinically labeled EEG data from children with absence epilepsy to identify co-occurrence patterns among discharge morphology, scalp distribution, and seizure duration. Key rules included polyspike-and-wave→spike-and-wave (confidence 1.000) and mesial temporal→central involvement (confidence 0.968), but the small single-center sample limits generalizability, so findings are exploratory.

papers.title: Mirtazapine and Slow-Wave Sleep: A Focused Narrative Review of Human Polysomnographic Evidence.
papers.summary: This focused narrative review examines mirtazapine's effects on sleep architecture, particularly slow-wave sleep, based on human polysomnographic evidence. It finds that while mirtazapine can measurably alter objective sleep, evidence for consistent enhancement of N3 or slow-wave sleep remains preliminary and mixed, with no established dose-response relationship.

papers.title: Emergency management of extreme hyperbilirubinemia.
papers.summary: This review provides guidance on the emergency management of extreme hyperbilirubinemia in neonates, emphasizing accurate monitoring to recognize bilirubin neurotoxicity using amplitude-integrated EEG and point-of-care ultrasound to guide vascular access. It also reviews exchange transfusion literature and proposes a classification of exchange transfusions based on vessels, catheters, and techniques.

papers.title: Valproate-Associated Hyperammonemic Encephalopathy Despite Nontoxic Serum Levels and Preserved Liver Function: A Case Report.
papers.summary: The paper reports a 49-year-old man with drug-resistant epilepsy who developed valproate-associated hyperammonemic encephalopathy (VHE) despite therapeutic or subtherapeutic valproate levels and preserved liver function. Valproate withdrawal led to sustained neurological recovery and a decrease in serum ammonia from 126.5 to 43.1 µmol/L.

papers.title: Roles in brain stimulation, recording and interpreting neuroimaging data: a systematic survey of 26 countries on current practices in EEG, MRI, TCD, TMS and FUS.
papers.summary: This systematic survey of 26 countries compiled local practices for performing and interpreting EEG, brain MRI, TMS, TCD, and FUS. It found that while some procedures have clear role definitions, there is a significant absence of local guidelines for responsibilities in performing and interpreting TMS and FUS, highlighting the need for standardized national protocols.

papers.title: Ictal laughter induced by repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation in stroke patients: a case series.
papers.summary: The paper presents two cases of acute ischemic stroke patients who developed stimulus-locked ictal laughter during low-frequency (1 Hz) rTMS applied to the left primary motor cortex for upper limb rehabilitation. Discontinuation of rTMS resulted in complete symptom resolution, and the authors suggest that low-frequency protocols may not be uniformly safe in post-stroke patients with structural brain lesions.

papers.title: Probable Sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease Presenting as Rapidly Progressive Dementia: A Case Report From Georgia.
papers.summary: The paper describes a 53-year-old man from Georgia with probable sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease presenting as rapidly progressive dementia, gait ataxia, and other neurological signs. Diagnosis was supported by a positive CSF 14-3-3 protein result and MRI restricted diffusion in the left caudate nucleus, but the patient died approximately seven months after symptom onset.

papers.title: A Four-Year Diagnostic Journey to Acute Intermittent Porphyria in a 19-Year-Old Woman: Lessons on Recognizing Neurovisceral Clues.
papers.summary: The paper reports a 19-year-old woman with a four-year history of recurrent seizures and abdominal pain who was ultimately diagnosed with acute intermittent porphyria (AIP) after fecal total porphyrins were found elevated at 72.3 nmol/g. It emphasizes that normal urinary porphyrin levels outside an acute attack do not exclude AIP and that fecal porphyrin analysis can provide complementary evidence.

papers.title: Functional Neurological Disorder Presenting as Psychogenic Non-epileptic Seizures Associated With Recurrent Hemoptysis: A Diagnostic Challenge.
papers.summary: This case report presents a 15-year-old male with psychogenic non-epileptic seizures (PNES) and recurrent hemoptysis, for whom extensive investigations revealed no organic cause. A diagnosis of functional neurological disorder was made, and the patient improved with psychotherapy, SSRIs, clonazepam, and tranexamic acid during hemoptysis episodes.

papers.title: Abrupt Termination of Severe Treatment Refractory Neuropsychiatric Symptoms in a Patient Treated With Rituximab-A Case Report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 65-year-old woman with severe treatment-refractory neuropsychiatric symptoms, including psychosis and cognitive decline, who was ultimately diagnosed with a possible systemic lupus erythematosus-related process. Following two 1-g rituximab infusions, she experienced substantial symptom reduction within 3 weeks and near-complete return to premorbid functioning within 6 months.

papers.title: [Psychocardiology-When cardiac rhythm meets psychological experience : Why cardiac arrhythmias elicit a psychological response].
papers.summary: This review discusses cardiac arrhythmias from a psychocardiological and psychosomatic perspective, emphasizing the heart-brain axis and the roles of anxiety, depression, hypervigilance, and illness perception. It uses atrial fibrillation as a model of a biopsychosocial disorder and advocates for an integrative clinical approach that considers both biological findings and subjective experience.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
